entries.title: Revelation of John 17:1
segments:
The sixth division of the book gives the vision of the harlot riding on the beast, and of the fall of Babylon.
 

 
 The great harlot. The harlot represents the faithless church, in her submission to the world.  In the prophetical sense, a harlot is one who has broken her marriage vows; Jerusalem and Judah thus broke their covenant vows with God.  See
.  Tyre and Nineveh were both called harlots in the Old Testament.  See

.
 

 
 Upon many waters.  Unstable and faithless.  See

entries.title: Revelation of John 17:2
segments: Drunken with the wine.

entries.title: Revelation of John 17:3
segments: In the spirit. See

, and note thereon.
 

 
 A scarlet-colored beast. This beast was, as before, the Roman empire, representing the world with its pomp and luxury.

entries.title: Revelation of John 17:4
segments: In purple and scarlet. The attire of a harlot, indicating luxury and pride.  Contrast this picture with the woman of
, the church in her first glory.

entries.title: Revelation of John 17:6
segments: Drunken with the blood. Referring to the madness of persecutions.  See

entries.title: Revelation of John 17:8
segments: Was, and is not. This probably refers to the power of Satan himself as manifested in the world-power.  He is the power of darkness (

 Out of the abyss. See

.
 

 
 Go into perdition. See

.
 

 
 That dwell on the earth. The ungodly shall admire and worship the pomp and pride of evil which panders to their own sin.  Thus it has always been, and is today.  But they whose names are written in the book of life will have their affection fixed on their Lord, and will not be deceived.
 

 
 Book of life. See

entries.title: Revelation of John 17:9
segments: The mind that hath wisdom. A caution that he is speaking enigmatically, and that only the saints will be able to understand.  This was probably on account of the persecutions of the church by the Jews and the Roman empire.  See

.
 

 
 Seven mountains. This passage must have some reference to Rome, which was built upon seven hills.  But it typifies all seats of evil power and political influence.  In this sense, the number (seven) of the mountains symbolizes universal power.

entries.title: Revelation of John 17:10
segments: Seven kings. Probably referring to seven of the Caesars; but the exact reference cannot be now determined.

entries.title: Revelation of John 17:12
segments: The ten horns. Perhaps some allied powers which aided imperial Rome in warning on Christianity.

entries.title: Revelation of John 17:14
segments: These shall war, etc.  The forces of evil, arrayed against Jesus and his kingdom, shall finally turn on the church, as she has become apostate, and shall bring her to ruin.

entries.title: Revelation of John 17:18
segments: The great city. There can hardly fail to be some reference here to Rome as the capital of the world.
